paper_metadata.title: Non-Differentiable Learning of Quantum Circuit Born Machine with Genetic Algorithm

summary: The paper evaluates a 12‑qubit quantum circuit Born machine (QCBM) with 84 variational parameters trained via a genetic algorithm to model financial return distributions. In simulations, the QCBM achieves a lower objective‑function error (mean 30.5, std 23.6 over 100 runs) than a comparable classical RBM baseline (mean 39.6, std 30.8) when generating samples from a 5,000‑point Gaussian mixture dataset, but all experiments are performed on a Qiskit simulator and do not demonstrate quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Training and evaluating a 12-qubit quantum circuit Born machine (QCBM) for generative modeling of two financial datasets, compared against a classical RBM baseline; QCBM trained with a genetic algorithm and simulated in Qiskit.

algorithm.variant: Quantum circuit Born machine (QCBM) trained with a genetic algorithm
algorithm.ansatz: Hardware-efficient parametrized quantum circuit with 3 layers of 1-qubit rotations and 2 layers of fixed 2-qubit entangling gates
algorithm.convergence_criteria: L = 200 generations; best objective value tracked across generations
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Randomly draw each rotation angle from the uniform distribution over the discrete angle set defined by m

optimizer_settings.parameter_bounds: rotation angles in [-pi, pi) discretized into 2^m values
optimizer_settings.selection: top M solutions retained each generation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Continuous samples are converted to 12-digit binary representation; each data sample becomes 12 binary features per variable representation
problem_formulation.objective_function: F(θ̂) = sum_{k=1..K} (u_k - v_k(θ̂))^2, where u and v are sorted training and generated samples

problem_instance.description: Generative modeling of financial and synthetic continuous distributions using binary-encoded samples
problem_instance.dataset_name: Mixture of four normal distributions, USD-JPY spot FX daily log-returns

dataset_specification.synthetic_dataset: 4-component Gaussian mixture with means [-3,-1,1,3], standard deviations [0.3,0.3,0.3,0.3], weights [0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4]

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Real-valued samples converted to 12-digit binary features using min-max scaling and integer binarization; generated binary outputs converted back to real values by inverse mapping
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: QCBM and RBM trained on the datasets; 5,000 samples generated for dataset 1 and 4,382 for dataset 2; 100 runs used for objective-function statistics on dataset 1; PDF and QQ plots used for qualitative evaluation

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Binary feature construction from real-valued data via min-max scaling and discretization
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Binary samples converted back to real-valued samples via inverse integer-to-real mapping

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: decreasing with diminishing returns as mutation rate decays

speedup_claims.factor: single circuit run per sample vs 10^3-10^4 forward/backward passes
speedup_claims.conditions: for generating an independent sample from the learned distribution; ignoring readout and other overheads
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a qualitative argument in the introduction, not an experimentally measured speedup.
The paper reports better objective-function statistics for QCBM than RBM, but does not quantify a runtime speedup.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not analyzed; the experiment uses a simulated 12‑qubit QCBM with 84 parameters and no scaling study toward larger systems.
limiting_factors: Experiment performed only on a classical simulator (Qiskit).
Very small system size (12 qubits, 84 parameters).
No runtime comparison or scaling analysis vs classical models.
Performance metric limited to distribution similarity objective.
Generative modeling task encoded with classical preprocessing.

notes: QCBM runs were performed on the Qiskit simulator; no real QPU device is named, so hardware.type is simulator_other.
Circuit depth inferred as 5 from the described architecture: 3 layers of adjustable 1-qubit gates plus 2 layers of fixed 2-qubit gates.
Speedup order is not characterized asymptotically in the paper; only speculative quantum advantage is discussed.
Table 1 shows QCBM objective mean 30.5 vs RBM 39.6, indicating slightly better performance on the metric.
The authors explicitly state this 'cannot be seen as evidence of quantum advantage'.
Both models successfully learn the distribution, so results indicate comparable performance rather than demonstrated advantage.
